title: Perimeter KMS policy enforcer and immutable audit envelope for private installer
author: Anais Lefevre
release_notes: Add perimeter KMS enforcement and immutable audit envelopes for private installs; opt-in via --enable-perimeter-kms flag; rolling upgrade instructions included.
description:
Motivation: Customers deploying Redwood Private need stronger guarantees that customer workloads use jurisdictionally-appropriate KMS providers and that audit records produced at install-time and runtime are tamper-evident. This PR introduces a perimeter KMS policy enforcer in the installer runtime and an immutable audit envelope writer that signs/salting audit payloads before sending to the central aggregator.

What this changes (single-string description): Adds an installer middleware that validates configured KMS provider bindings against a per-tenant jurisdiction policy template (templates/kms-residency/*.yaml). The enforcer runs during both: (a) initial install validation and (b) runtime operator credential handoff when the private control plane boots. When a KMS binding violates residency rules the installer fails fast and emits a descriptive remediation hint. In parallel we introduce audit-envelopes: audit payloads are wrapped with a canonicalized header, timestamp, and an HMAC over the payload using a rotation-capable signing key stored in the local keystore. Envelopes are marked immutable; the edge forwarder will reject any audit record that does not verify.

Design notes: The enforcer uses OPA-style policy templates but ships a tiny policy engine (policy/engine.go) that evaluates residency predicates offline so the installer is self-contained for air-gapped customers. KMS selection supports multi-provider rules (aws:kms, gcp:cloudkms, hsm:local) and a fallback preference list when multi-provider consent is enabled. There is also a compatibility shim to opt-out (environment variable REDWOOD_PERIMETER_KMS=disabled) for older installs; default for new installer releases is enabled.

Security considerations: The audit envelope signing includes a nonce and provenance metadata (installer-version, host-fingerprint, tenant-id) to reduce replay risk. Signing keys are seeded from the installer keystore and can be rotated via the new subcommand installer key rotate. The enforcer logs minimal information on policy failures (policy id, reason) and only emits tenant-level identifiers to support incident triage.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests for policy engine and envelope verification included. Added integration tests that exercise a three-node private control plane in acceptance harness (ci/integration/kms-perimeter). Rollout plan: default feature-flag = enabled for new images; staged canary via the installer channel and a 2-week telemetry check before global enable.

How to review: scan policy templates under templates/kms-residency, read policy engine (policy/engine.go), and inspect installer hooks (installer/hook/kms_enforcer.go) and audit envelope code (audit/envelope.go). Important: the e2e harness files under ci/integration were expanded to include an offline KMS mock.

Checklist:
- [x] Policy engine implementation and unit tests
- [x] Immutable audit envelope writer and verification tests
- [x] Integration tests with KMS mock harness
- [x] Docs and upgrade notes (docs/private-installer/kms-perimeter.md)

Notes: This is purposely conservative in scope (installer + forwarder + local policy engine). Future follow-ups: (1) central policy management UI sync, (2) runtime enforcement inside private control plane long-running process, (3) hardened HSM integration for signing keys.

review_comments: Diego Marquez: +1 on the design; please add a small debug log when a binding is auto-rewritten by the fallback rule so operators can see the change. — Author: added ephemeral.debug log and note in upgrade docs (commit 4)

Rohit Patel: Concern about diffing canonicalization causing false negatives on envelope verification. — Author: canonicalization is now strict JSON canonical form with sorted keys; added roundtrip test to envelope_test.go
Marta Ivanova: Please enumerate possible false positives for residency templates (e.g., overlapping regions). — Author: updated templates and added validation routine to templates/validate.go
merge_outcome: Merged via squash merge after second approval. Post-merge: created deployment tag private-installer@v1.12.0-perimeter-kms
notes_for_operators: Upgrade path: run installer --validate on existing manifests to detect any policy violations; use installer key rotate to pre-seed signing keys for audit envelopes. To temporarily disable enforcement set REDWOOD_PERIMETER_KMS=disabled until policies are reconciled.
upgrade_instructions: 1) Run installer --validate to surface residency violations. 2) Resolve or add consent entries in templates/kms-residency. 3) Re-run installer with --enable-perimeter-kms. For air-gapped installs, ensure templates are present in the bundle. See docs/private-installer/kms-perimeter.md for examples.
security_review_summary: Security reviewed by SecOps (Rohit Patel). Key outcomes: signing key lifecycle added, canonicalization hardened, limited PII in failure logs. No unresolved findings.
